extracted.intended_audience: petitioners, patent owners, and counsel participating in PTAB IPR and PGR proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: USPTO guidance describing the Director's interim discretionary process for institution decisions in inter partes review (IPR) and post-grant review (PGR), including what considerations may be raised, briefing rules, timing, filing mechanics, and decision procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's holistic review authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has broad authority to determine whether to exercise discretion to institute an IPR or PGR; decisions are based on a holistic review of facts and circumstances and may consider PTAB precedent, the Consolidated Trial Practice Guide, the Process Memorandum, and any other fact or circumstance a party believes bears on discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will ordinarily rely on facts and circumstances the parties raise in briefs but may consider additional facts (e.g., matters within the Office's purview or public-domain facts). The Director's decision may highlight certain considerations and will explain why discretionary denial was or was not appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplary discretionary considerations — prior adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the PTAB or another forum has already adjudicated the validity or patentability of the challenged patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are encouraged to raise any facts showing prior adjudication as bearing on the Director's discretion (e.g., final judgments, earlier trial results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplary discretionary considerations — changes in law or precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there have been changes in the law or new judicial precedent issued since issuance of the claims that may affect patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may cite recent judicial decisions or statutory/regulatory changes that materially alter the patentability landscape for the challenged claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplary discretionary considerations — strength of the unpatentability challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: The strength of the petitioner's unpatentability challenge as a factor weighing for or against discretionary institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should explain, with facts/evidence, why the merits appear strong or weak; note that merits must primarily be developed in the petition/POPR and Director will consult technical personnel as needed when assessing merits arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplary discretionary considerations — extent of reliance on expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: How heavily the petition relies on expert testimony is an exemplary consideration for discretionary denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may point out an undue reliance on expert opinion (or lack thereof) as affecting the strength or appropriateness of institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplary discretionary considerations — settled expectations of the parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Settled expectations of the parties, such as the length of time the claims have been in force, may weigh in discretionary decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners may emphasize reliance interests or long-standing market expectations; petitioners may rebut such arguments in their opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplary discretionary considerations — compelling public/economic/ national security interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Compelling economic, public health, or national security interests are factors that may support discretionary denial or institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should identify and support any such public-interest considerations with facts and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplary discretionary considerations — other non-exhaustive factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Process Memorandum lists non-exhaustive considerations (including Fintiv, General Plastic, Advanced Bionics, and guidance from the Consolidated Trial Practice Guide) and the Director may consider any other circumstances bearing on discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are encouraged to raise any fact or circumstance they believe bears on discretion, including considerations not explicitly discussed in precedent or the Process Memorandum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of discretionary vs. merits arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must present merits and other non-discretionary arguments (with evidence) in the petition, Patent Owner Preliminary Response (POPR), and authorized replies; discretionary considerations should not be presented in the petition or the POPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Board panel will consider only arguments and evidence cited in the petition/POPR for merits determinations. When addressing discretionary briefs, parties may direct attention to merits evidence but should not treat discretionary briefing as an extra merits opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner discretionary denial brief — availability and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners in proceedings with POPR deadlines after March 26, 2025 may file a discretionary denial brief; it must be filed within two months of the Notice of Filing Date Accorded (NFDA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may not stipulate to a later due date for the patent owner discretionary denial brief in order to protect statutory deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner discretionary denial brief — content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner should argue with particularity the circumstances that warrant discretionary denial, relying on PTAB precedent, Consolidated Trial Practice Guide, Process Memorandum, and any other considerations the patent owner believes bear on discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners may direct attention to an anticipated POPR and cite record evidence, but should not repeat merits arguments verbatim; the brief should be a focused explanation of why discretionary denial is warranted, supported by facts and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner discretionary denial brief — evidence and incorporation limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners may submit evidence in support of discretionary arguments and may refer to anticipated POPR material despite the prohibition on incorporation by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director will consider the petition, the POPR, and evidence cited therein when determining discretionary denial; patent owners should ensure key merits evidence is properly of record in the petition/POPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner discretionary denial brief — page/word limits and requests for additional pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective for discretionary denial requests due on/after Sept 1, 2025, patent owner briefs are limited to 20 pages; for briefs due before that date the limit per Process Memorandum is 14,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may request additional pages but must demonstrate good cause for extra pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner's opposition brief — availability and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner should raise discretionary issues in its opposition to the patent owner's discretionary denial brief; the opposition must be filed within three months of the NFDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition itself should not address discretionary issues; parties may not stipulate to extend the opposition due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner's opposition brief — content and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner's brief should be responsive to the patent owner's discretionary arguments, raise discretionary issues (e.g., 35 U.S.C. § 325(d), parallel proceedings, serial petitions), and explain why the Office should institute review despite those considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners may direct attention to their petition and evidence for merits discussion but should not repeat merits arguments verbatim; they may submit evidence in support of discretionary positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner's opposition brief — page/word limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective for discretionary denial requests due on/after Sept 1, 2025, petitioners' oppositions are limited to 20 pages; for briefs due before that date the limit per Process Memorandum is 14,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners may request additional pages and must show good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulations and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petitioner files a stipulation (e.g., a Sotera stipulation), it should be filed as soon as practicable so the patent owner can address its impact in a discretionary denial brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will consider whether the stipulation materially reduces overlap between proceedings; stipulations may be less meaningful if the petitioner relies on corresponding system art in co-pending proceedings or on multiple invalidity theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional briefing (replies and sur-replies) — authorization standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies and sur-replies to discretionary briefs are not authorized by default; a party must demonstrate good cause to obtain authorization to file a reply or sur-reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should request authorization as soon as practicable by emailing Director_Discretionary_Decision@USPTO.gov with a copy to opposing counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file discretionary briefs (P-TACTS paper types and steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: After PTAB issues NFDA (or Notice of Defective Petition) and accepts Mandatory Notice, the paper types 'PO Discretionary Denial Brief' (for patent owners) and 'PET Opposition to Discretionary Denial Brief' (for petitioners) will be available in P-TACTS; parties must select the appropriate paper type and complete required fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step-by-step instructions: log into P-TACTS, go to My Docket → open case viewer → '+Add' → File Other Document modal → select the correct paper type → fill required fields (red asterisk) → Add to List → Submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional process — patent owner may decline to file
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner is not required to file a discretionary denial brief; if it chooses not to, the Director typically will not issue a discretionary decision and responsibility will pass to a Board panel the day after the due date for such a brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Office refers the case to a Board panel, a docket notice will be entered and the Board will decide institution on merits and non-discretionary issues raised in the petition/POPR and any authorized additional briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'merits' and examples of non-discretionary considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Merits considerations concern whether there is a reasonable likelihood the petitioner would prevail on at least one challenged claim (IPR), whether a patent is eligible for PGR, or whether it is more likely than not that at least one claim is unpatentable in PGR, or whether a PGR raises novel/unsettled legal questions important to other patents/applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-discretionary considerations include statutory and procedural requirements (e.g., 35 U.S.C. §§311, 312, 315(a),(b),(e), 322, 325(a),(e)), number/sufficiency of grounds, claim construction issues, meeting 37 C.F.R. §42.104(b), and relevant PTAB informative decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board handling of procedural motions unrelated to discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will decide procedural motions that do not relate to discretionary considerations regardless of when those motions are filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should file procedural motions with the Board as required; the timing of such motions does not affect the Director's discretionary review of discretionary briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director decision process, consultation, timing, and delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will receive each petition, discretionary denial brief, opposition, and POPR and will determine, in consultation with at least three senior PTAB judges (separate from merits judges), whether discretionary denial is appropriate; the Director may consult other USPTO employees without conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent good cause, the Director will issue a decision within one month of the due date of the last relevant paper filed. Decisions will either deny the petition or refer it to the Board and will explain the reasons. Authority delegated to Deputy Director for discretionary decisions; further delegation noted for conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of merits by Director and deference by Board
rubrics_metrics.description: When parties present strength-of-merits arguments, the Director will consult USPTO technical personnel; a Board panel is not bound by the Director's merits assessment and must explain differing findings in its institution decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board reaches different conclusions than the Director about merits, the panel must cite the parties' evidence of record as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for rehearing or Director Review and changed circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director denies institution on discretionary grounds, a party may file a request for rehearing or Director Review within 30 days; Director Review requests must follow 37 C.F.R. §42.75(c) and include the fee per 37 C.F.R. §42.15(f). If the Director declines discretionary denial, a party should wait and file a single request after the Board panel issues its decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changed circumstances (e.g., change in trial date) may be raised in a rehearing or Director Review filed within the applicable time period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest and recusal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director, a consulting PTAB member, or any USPTO employee has a conflict of interest, they shall recuse themselves; USPTO follows 5 C.F.R. Part 2635 and consults Department of Commerce ethics as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts may include prior involvement in examination or prosecution of the underlying or related patent. PTAB judges consulting with the Director also follow PTAB SOP 1. Delegation of authority procedures apply when delegates have conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locating Director Discretionary Decisions in PTAB records
rubrics_metrics.description: Director Discretionary Decisions are entered into the proceeding record and can be found on the PTAB webpage by searching Document type 'Director Discretionary Decision' and selecting both 'Refer' and 'Deny'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: Select 'All PTAB decision data' → 'Documents' tab → search for 'Director Discretionary Decision' under Document type → select both 'Refer' and 'Deny' → Apply.
